name: Nuclear plant safety
value: ZNPP power cut 8 Nov; worker killed 9 Nov
summary: Zaporizhzhia lost off-site power on 8 Nov and a worker was killed by a drone on 9 Nov; IAEA warns of winter grid risk
state: Zaporizhzhia lost its 330kV off-site power line on 8 Nov and ran on emergency diesel generators until the connection was restored, which the IAEA called the plant's 27th loss of off-site power of the conflict (Interfax-Ukraine). A plant worker was killed in a drone attack on 9 Nov, the second in under two weeks (United24), and on 15 Nov IAEA Director General Grossi warned that grid risks may increase in winter (APA). No damage to safety-critical systems, INES level 2 event or radiological release was found as of 19 Nov.
for_you: No radiation risk to the UK or Europe has been reported. Official information on any nuclear incident comes from the IAEA and national regulators.
rubric_hit: Watch: Zaporizhzhia lost all off-site power on 8 Nov; no safety-system damage or INES 2+ event (Alert)

why: Fighting near nuclear power plants risks a radiological release; the IAEA reports on Zaporizhzhia and other plants in or near war zones.
drivers: Off-site power losses, strikes near plants, staffing, cooling water, military occupation.

rubric.alert: Damage to safety-critical systems, an INES level 2 or higher event, or a radiological release.
rubric.watch: A plant loses all off-site power, strikes land near a plant, or the IAEA reports a deteriorating safety situation.
rubric.normal: No new IAEA safety concerns at plants in or near conflict zones.
